_about: Global sea level, in metres against today's, by years ago — for maps that show time (CWVault/claude/Spec-Maps.md, Time on the map). Read from the global, ice-volume-equivalent curve of Lambeck, Rouby, Purcell, Sun and Sambridge, 'Sea level and global ice volumes from the Last Glacial Maximum to the Holocene', PNAS 111 (43): 15296–15303 (2014), and rounded: approximate, and to be checked against the paper's supplementary table before a story leans on a particular number. A single global figure: the land also rose where the ice left, most in Scandinavia and around Hudson Bay, and this does not show that. The fast rise near 14,500 years ago is Meltwater Pulse 1A. Between points, interpolate linearly.
